subject: bias correction approach for direct and indirect effects, and OR calculation

messages.author: 1c40f1e00bf21a35
messages.subject: bias correction approach for direct and indirect effects, and OR calculation
parts:
Hi, I've been using the approach set out by Yves in a 2013 presentation to correct naive estimates ( see slides 25-27 in http://www.da.ugent.be/cvs/pages/en/Presentations/Presentation%20Yves%20Rosseel.pdf )

My code is:

load("dat3.Rdata")
str(dat3)
# lavaan model following Rosseel 2013 http://www.da.ugent.be/cvs/pages/en/Presentations/Presentation%20Yves%20Rosseel.pdf
# (slides 25-27) to calculate corrected estimates for direct and indirect effects, plus ORs
model1 <- '
 # regressions
  outcome ~ cprime*exposure + b*mediator
  mediator ~ a*exposure
 # variances and covariances
 # direct, indirect and total effects
  ab := (a * b)
 # label threshold for outcome
  outcome | b0*t1
  probit11 := (-b0+cprime+b*a)/sqrt(b^2+1)
  probit10 := (-b0+cprime )/sqrt(b^2+1)
  probit00 := (-b0 )/sqrt(b^2+1)
  indirect := pnorm(probit11) - pnorm(probit10)
  direct := pnorm(probit10) - pnorm(probit00)
  OR.indirect := (pnorm(probit11)/(1-pnorm(probit11)))/
                 (pnorm(probit10)/(1-pnorm(probit10)))
  OR.direct := (pnorm(probit10)/(1-pnorm(probit10)))/
               (pnorm(probit00)/(1-pnorm(probit00)))
'
fit1 <- sem(model1, data=dat3, ordered=c("outcome"), estimator = "WLSMV")
summary(fit1)
parameterEstimates(fit1, ci = TRUE, level = 0.95,
 boot.ci.type = "perc", standardized = T)[,c(1,2,4,5:10)]


The model runs ok and provides these estimates:


           lhs  op       label    est    se      z pvalue ci.lower ci.upper
1      outcome   ~      cprime -0.274 0.124 -2.208  0.027   -0.517   -0.031
2      outcome   ~           b -0.122 0.040 -3.044  0.002   -0.200   -0.043
3     mediator   ~           a  0.218 0.134  1.624  0.104   -0.045    0.482
4      outcome   |          b0 -0.170 0.250 -0.679  0.497   -0.660    0.320
5      outcome  ~~              0.968 0.000     NA     NA    0.968    0.968
6     mediator  ~~              2.162 0.142 15.172  0.000    1.882    2.441
7      outcome ~*~              1.000 0.000     NA     NA    1.000    1.000
8      outcome  ~1              0.000 0.000     NA     NA    0.000    0.000
9     mediator  ~1              5.811 0.103 56.405  0.000    5.609    6.013
10          ab  :=          ab -0.027 0.019 -1.432  0.152   -0.063    0.010
11    probit11  :=    probit11 -0.130 0.250 -0.519  0.604   -0.619    0.360
12    probit10  :=    probit10 -0.103 0.257 -0.401  0.688   -0.607    0.401
13    probit00  :=    probit00  0.169 0.248  0.682  0.496   -0.317    0.654
14    indirect  :=    indirect -0.010 0.007 -1.412  0.158   -0.025    0.004
15      direct  :=      direct -0.108 0.049 -2.216  0.027   -0.204   -0.013
16 OR.indirect  := OR.indirect  0.959 0.028 34.187  0.000    0.904    1.014
17   OR.direct  :=   OR.direct  0.648 0.128  5.074  0.000    0.398    0.898


I'm struggling to understand, though, why there is such a difference in the z score and p value for the direct / indirect effect estimates compared with the ORs for these? Any help with this would be appreciated.

David

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: bias correction approach for direct and indirect effects, and OR calculation
parts:
The z statistic and p-value are testing the null hypothesis that the parameter is equal to 0. For the direct and indirect effects a null finding is one where the parameter equals 0, for the OR a null finding is when the OR = 1. Thus the given p-values for the OR aren't testing a reasonable hypothesis (to get even more specific, the z statistic and it's p-value assume the sampling distribution of the parameter is normal, which isn't true for OR, they're bounded by 0, so it isn't an appropriate test here). 

Alex
